--- title: "Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?" subtitle: "What Census data tells us about seniors and younger adults living with a disability, from La Jolla to Chula Vista to El Cajon." description: "A look at Census data on seniors and younger adults who need help with daily life, across San Diego, from North City to the South Bay and East County." date: 2026-11-02 categories: [Research, Seniors, Disability, San Diego] --- ::: {.lead} When we started Marquez Family Home Care, we wanted to understand our neighbors before we knocked on a single door. Who in our community needs help at home, and what kind of help? We went to the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey for answers. ::: We looked at two groups we care for: - **Seniors (65 and older)** who want to stay safe and comfortable in the home they know. - **Younger adults (18 to 64) living with a disability**, including people with developmental disabilities and people recovering from a brain or spinal cord injury. The Census doesn't ask whether someone "needs a caregiver." It asks about specific difficulties, and two of them line up closely with non-medical home care: | Census question | What it means day to day | In this post we call it | How a caregiver helps | |---|---|---|---| | **Self-care difficulty** | Trouble bathing or dressing | **Need personal care help** | Personal care, done with dignity | | **Independent-living difficulty** | Trouble running errands or getting to appointments alone | **Need errand help** | Companionship, errands, rides, meals, light housekeeping | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(tidycensus) library(scales) library(knitr) library(sf) library(leaflet) options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE) # ACS 5-year vintage. 2024 = the 2020–2024 survey. Drop to 2023 if load_variables() errors. acs_year <- 2024 # Neighborhoods we serve, grouped into four regions (ZIP code tabulation areas) region_levels <- c("Central & North City", "Central San Diego", "South Bay", "East County") service_area <- tribble( ~zcta, ~region, ~area, # Central & North City: around our home base in University City (92122) "92122", "Central & North City", "University City", "92037", "Central & North City", "La Jolla", "92117", "Central & North City", "Clairemont", "92111", "Central & North City", "Linda Vista / Kearny Mesa", "92123", "Central & North City", "Serra Mesa", "92124", "Central & North City", "Tierrasanta", "92126", "Central & North City", "Mira Mesa", "92121", "Central & North City", "Sorrento Valley", "92130", "Central & North City", "Carmel Valley", "92129", "Central & North City", "Rancho Peñasquitos", "92131", "Central & North City", "Scripps Ranch", "92109", "Central & North City", "Pacific Beach", "92110", "Central & North City", "Bay Park / Morena", "92108", "Central & North City", "Mission Valley", "92120", "Central & North City", "Allied Gardens / Del Cerro", "92119", "Central & North City", "San Carlos", "92128", "Central & North City", "Rancho Bernardo", "92014", "Central & North City", "Del Mar", # Central San Diego: Mid-City, downtown, southeast and the coast west of downtown "92101", "Central San Diego", "Downtown / Little Italy", "92103", "Central San Diego", "Hillcrest / Mission Hills", "92104", "Central San Diego", "North Park", "92116", "Central San Diego", "Normal Heights / Kensington", "92115", "Central San Diego", "College Area / Rolando", "92105", "Central San Diego", "City Heights", "92102", "Central San Diego", "Golden Hill / Sherman Heights", "92113", "Central San Diego", "Logan Heights / Barrio Logan", "92114", "Central San Diego", "Encanto / Skyline", "92139", "Central San Diego", "Paradise Hills / Bay Terraces", "92106", "Central San Diego", "Point Loma", "92107", "Central San Diego", "Ocean Beach", # South Bay "91902", "South Bay", "Bonita", "91910", "South Bay", "Chula Vista (northwest)", "91911", "South Bay", "Chula Vista (southwest)", "91913", "South Bay", "Chula Vista (Eastlake / Otay Ranch)", "91914", "South Bay", "Chula Vista (Eastlake northeast)", "91915", "South Bay", "Chula Vista (Eastlake Greens)", "91950", "South Bay", "National City", "91932", "South Bay", "Imperial Beach", "92154", "South Bay", "Otay Mesa / Nestor", "92173", "South Bay", "San Ysidro", # East County "91941", "East County", "La Mesa / Mount Helix", "91942", "East County", "La Mesa", "91945", "East County", "Lemon Grove", "91977", "East County", "Spring Valley", "91978", "East County", "Spring Valley (east)", "92020", "East County", "El Cajon (west)", "92021", "East County", "El Cajon (east)", "92019", "East County", "El Cajon (Rancho San Diego)", "92071", "East County", "Santee" ) |> mutate(region = factor(region, levels = region_levels)) service_zips <- service_area$zcta if (Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY") == "") { stop("No Census API key found. Run tidycensus::census_api_key('YOUR_KEY', install = TRUE) and restart R.") } # Brand colors for charts brand <- list( forest = "#0f3e17", petal = "#79b88b", burgundy = "#7a1f3d", cream = "#fffefc", charcoal = "#222222", mist = "#efeeeb" ) band_labels <- c(u18 = "Under 18", a18_64 = "Adults 18–64", s65 = "Seniors 65+") band_colors <- c("Adults 18–64" = brand$petal, "Seniors 65+" = brand$forest) measure_labels <- c( any = "Any disability", selfcare = "Need personal care help", indliving = "Need errand help" ) theme_marquez <- function(base_size = 12) { theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + theme( text = element_text(color = brand$charcoal), plot.title = element_text(color = brand$forest, size = base_size + 3), plot.title.position = "plot", plot.subtitle = element_text(color = brand$charcoal), plot.caption = element_text(color = brand$charcoal, size = base_size - 3, hjust = 0), plot.caption.position = "plot", strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, color = brand$forest, face = "bold"), panel.spacing.y = unit(14, "pt"), axis.text = element_text(color = brand$charcoal), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = brand$mist), legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", plot.background = element_rect(fill = brand$cream, color = NA), panel.background = element_rect(fill = brand$cream, color = NA) ) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} acs_vars <- load_variables(acs_year, "acs5", cache = TRUE) |> select(name, label) |> mutate(label = str_remove_all(label, ":")) acs_pull <- function(level = c("county", "zcta"), table = NULL, variables = NULL) { level <- match.arg(level) args <- list(year = acs_year, survey = "acs5") if (!is.null(table)) args$table <- table if (!is.null(variables)) args$variables <- variables args <- if (level == "county") { c(args, geography = "county", state = "CA", county = "San Diego") } else { c(args, list(geography = "zcta", zcta = service_zips)) } out <- do.call(get_acs, args) if (!is.null(table)) out <- left_join(out, acs_vars, by = c("variable" = "name")) out } last_part <- function(label) word(label, -1, sep = "!!") age_band <- function(age) { case_when( age %in% c("Under 18 years", "5 to 17 years") ~ "u18", age %in% c("18 to 34 years", "35 to 64 years", "18 to 64 years") ~ "a18_64", age %in% c("65 to 74 years", "75 years and over", "65 years and over") ~ "s65", TRUE ~ NA_character_ ) } # Population by age (B01001) age_counts <- function(level) { acs_pull(level, table = "B01001") |> filter(str_count(label, "!!") == 3) |> mutate( age_txt = last_part(label), age_lo = if_else(str_detect(age_txt, "^Under"), 0, as.numeric(str_extract(age_txt, "\\d+"))) ) |> group_by(GEOID, NAME) |> summarise( pop_total = sum(estimate), pop_18_64 = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 18 & age_lo < 65]), pop_65 = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 65]), pop_75 = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 75]), pop_85 = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 85]), .groups = "drop" ) } # Disability / difficulty status by age band (C18108, B18106, B18107), parsed by label status_by_age <- function(level, table, leaf_pattern, without_pattern) { acs_pull(level, table = table) |> filter(str_detect(last_part(label), leaf_pattern)) |> mutate( age = str_extract(label, "Under 18 years|\\d+ to \\d+ years|\\d+ years and over"), band = age_band(age), has = !str_detect(last_part(label), without_pattern) ) |> filter(!is.na(band)) |> group_by(GEOID, band) |> summarise( with = sum(estimate[has]), with_moe = moe_sum(moe[has], estimate[has]), universe = sum(estimate), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate(pct = with / universe) } status_long <- function(level) { bind_rows( any = status_by_age(level, "C18108", "disability", "^No disability"), selfcare = status_by_age(level, "B18106", "difficulty", "^No "), indliving = status_by_age(level, "B18107", "difficulty", "^No "), .id = "measure" ) } status_wide <- function(long) { long |> select(GEOID, measure, band, with, pct) |> pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, band), values_from = c(with, pct), names_glue = "{measure}_{band}_{.value}") } # Seniors living alone (B09020) living_alone <- function(level) { acs_pull(level, table = "B09020") |> group_by(GEOID) |> summarise( pop65_universe = estimate[variable == "B09020_001"], alone_65 = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, regex("living alone$", ignore_case = TRUE))]), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate(pct_alone_65 = alone_65 / pop65_universe) } # Spanish spoken at home among people 65+ (B16004) spanish_65 <- function(level) { acs_pull(level, table = "B16004") |> group_by(GEOID) |> summarise( pop65_lang = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, "!!65 years and over$")]), spanish_65 = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, "65 years and over!!Speak Spanish$")]), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate(pct_spanish_65 = spanish_65 / pop65_lang) } build_profile <- function(level) { long <- status_long(level) wide <- list(age_counts(level), status_wide(long), living_alone(level), spanish_65(level)) |> reduce(left_join, by = "GEOID") list(wide = wide, long = long) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} county_raw <- build_profile("county") zip_raw <- build_profile("zcta") county <- county_raw$wide county_long <- county_raw$long zips <- zip_raw$wide |> left_join(service_area, by = c("GEOID" = "zcta")) zip_long <- zip_raw$long |> left_join(service_area, by = c("GEOID" = "zcta")) # When the numbers were pulled from the Census API (kept with the frozen results) data_pulled <- Sys.Date() pulled_label <- sprintf("%s %d, %s", format(data_pulled, "%B"), as.integer(format(data_pulled, "%d")), format(data_pulled, "%Y")) acs_label <- paste0("American Community Survey ", acs_year - 4, "–", acs_year, " 5-year estimates") source_caption <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, ".") ``` ::: ## San Diego County at a glance ::: {.stat-grid} ::: {.stat} [507,734]{.stat-number} [residents aged 65 and older]{.stat-label} ::: ::: {.stat} [59,830]{.stat-number} [residents aged 85 and older]{.stat-label} ::: ::: {.stat} [136,323]{.stat-number} [adults who need errand help]{.stat-label} ::: ::: {.stat} [122,505]{.stat-number} [seniors who live alone]{.stat-label} ::: ::: ::: {.data-note} Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates. Data pulled from the Census on November 2, 2026. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tribble( ~` `, ~`Adults 18–64`, ~`Seniors 65+`, "People in the county", comma(county$pop_18_64), comma(county$pop_65), "Living with any disability", comma(county$any_a18_64_with), comma(county$any_s65_with), "Need personal care help", comma(county$selfcare_a18_64_with), comma(county$selfcare_s65_with), "Need errand help", comma(county$indliving_a18_64_with), comma(county$indliving_s65_with) ) |> kable(caption = paste0("San Diego County, ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, ".")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: San Diego County, American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates. Data pulled November 2, 2026. | |Adults 18–64 |Seniors 65+ | |:--------------------------|:------------|:-----------| |People in the county |2,093,723 |507,734 | |Living with any disability |169,980 |157,192 | |Need personal care help |28,185 |41,237 | |Need errand help |61,986 |74,337 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} county_long |> filter(band %in% c("a18_64", "s65")) |> mutate(measure = factor(measure_labels[measure], levels = rev(measure_labels)), band = band_labels[band]) |> ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = measure, fill = band)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct, 0.1)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4, color = brand$charcoal) + scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + scale_fill_manual(values = band_colors) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "The need for help grows with age, but it isn't only about age") + labs(caption = source_caption) + theme_marquez() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/county-chart-1.png){fig-alt='Bar chart comparing the share of adults 18 to 64 and seniors 65 and over in San Diego County with any disability, needing personal care help, and needing errand help.' width=672} ::: ::: Seniors are several times more likely than younger adults to need help with daily tasks. But because there are so many more adults under 65, **younger adults with a disability are a large share of the people who need a hand at home**. Home care isn't only for grandparents. > Often the hardest part of needing help is the everyday: getting to the doctor, a hot meal, > a ride to the store. Those are the moments we're here for. ## Neighborhood by neighborhood We serve four parts of the county: the neighborhoods around our home base in University City, central San Diego from downtown to Mid-City and the southeast, the South Bay, and East County. Here's how they compare. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} zips |> group_by(Region = region) |> summarise( `ZIP codes` = n(), `Seniors 65+` = sum(pop_65), `Seniors 85+` = sum(pop_85), `Living alone (65+)` = sum(alone_65) / sum(pop65_universe), `Need errand help (65+)` = sum(indliving_s65_with), `Need errand help (18–64)` = sum(indliving_a18_64_with), `Spanish at home (65+)` = sum(spanish_65) / sum(pop65_lang), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate( across(c(`Seniors 65+`, `Seniors 85+`, `Need errand help (65+)`, `Need errand help (18–64)`), comma), across(c(`Living alone (65+)`, `Spanish at home (65+)`), \(x) percent(x, 0.1)) ) |> kable(align = "lrrrrrrr", caption = paste0("Totals for the ZIP codes we serve. ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, ".")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Totals for the ZIP codes we serve. American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates. Data pulled November 2, 2026. |Region | ZIP codes| Seniors 65+| Seniors 85+| Living alone (65+)| Need errand help (65+)| Need errand help (18–64)| Spanish at home (65+)| |:--------------------|---------:|-----------:|-----------:|------------------:|----------------------:|------------------------:|---------------------:| |Central & North City | 18| 112,946| 15,223| 24.9%| 15,304| 9,034| 6.1%| |Central San Diego | 12| 71,681| 7,232| 30.6%| 12,413| 10,733| 20.5%| |South Bay | 10| 67,559| 8,741| 18.7%| 13,228| 10,708| 44.1%| |East County | 9| 65,645| 7,557| 22.8%| 10,021| 10,847| 11.4%| ::: ::: ### Explore the map Choose a measure, then hover over (or tap) a neighborhood to see its numbers. Darker green means more people, or a higher share, for that measure. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ZIP code boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGER/Line cartographic files) zip_geo <- get_acs( geography = "zcta", zcta = service_zips, variables = "B01001_001", year = acs_year, survey = "acs5", geometry = TRUE ) |> select(GEOID, geometry) |> st_transform(4326) # Share of adults (18+) with an independent-living difficulty need_rate <- zip_long |> filter(measure == "indliving", band %in% c("a18_64", "s65")) |> group_by(GEOID) |> summarise(need_n = sum(with), need_universe = sum(universe), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(need_pct = need_n / need_universe) map_data <- zip_geo |> left_join(zips, by = "GEOID") |> left_join(need_rate, by = "GEOID") |> mutate(hover = sprintf( "%s · %s
%s

South Bay, and East County, split into adults 18 to 64 and seniors 65 and over.' width=672} ::: ::: ## What this means for families ::: {.panel-keylime} **Many families in our area are caring for someone right now**, often while working full time. A few things stood out to us: - **Help with everyday tasks is the most common need.** More people need errand help than need personal care help. Companionship, rides and meals matter. - **Younger adults need support too.** Developmental disabilities and injuries from accidents affect people at every age. The San Diego Regional Center alone serves about 41,350 people with developmental disabilities across San Diego and Imperial counties. - **Language matters.** In parts of the South Bay, a large share of seniors speak Spanish at home. A caregiver who speaks your loved one's language makes care feel like home. ::: ## Why we're building this ::: {.panel-blush} We didn't start Marquez Family Home Care to compete with the agencies already caring for San Diego families. We started it because the need keeps growing. Every year, more of our neighbors reach the age when everyday tasks get harder, and more younger adults are living with a disability or recovering from an injury. Many families are already stretched thin. Our goal is to help fill that gap, alongside everyone else doing this work, so that more people can stay safe, comfortable and independent in the homes they love. ::: ::: {.cta-panel} ### Wondering whether your loved one could use some help? We're happy to talk it through, with no pressure and no obligation. Marquez Family Home Care provides non-medical support: personal care, companionship, meals, errands and respite for family caregivers. Regional Center figure: San Diego Regional Center FY 2023–24 Performance Report, CA Department of Developmental Services. - **People living in nursing homes aren't included**, which suits our purpose: these are people living in their own homes. - **Neighborhood numbers are estimates** with real margins of error, especially in smaller ZIP codes. Treat the ranking as a general picture, not an exact count. - **The measures overlap.** Someone who needs personal care help often needs errand help too, so the rows shouldn't be added together. - **ZIP areas are approximate.** The Census uses "ZIP code tabulation areas," which closely match, but don't exactly equal, postal ZIP codes.
